segments.t: At the ASK agency, Catherine Barneville drops by to visit Noemie, who is wearing a neck brace. When Mathias arrives, Catherine reveals she has invited Noemie over for dinner with her handsome physical therapist. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Catherine, tu voulais me voir?
Non mon chéri, je viens voir Noémie.
Elle porte un corset depuis quinze jours.
Oui, elle doit bien se reposer.
Je la trouve vraiment très rayonnante.
C'est gentil d'être passée à l'agence.
Je l'ai invitée à dîner ce soir.
Tu l'as invitée chez nous?
Oui, avec quelques amis très sympathiques.
Mon kiné Alexandre sera là aussi.
Tu penses que c'est une bonne idée?
Il est charmant et extrêmement doué.
Il va beaucoup l'aider pour sa rééducation.
D'accord, nous verrons bien ce soir.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Catherine, tu voulais me voir?
'Catherine, did you want to see me?' Mathias asks his wife about her visit. The informal 'you' form around 'wanted' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Non mon chéri, je viens voir Noémie.
'No my darling, I am visiting Noemie.' Catherine explains she came to see Noemie. The verb meaning 'come' pairs naturally with the noun for 'darling' in everyday conversation.
Elle porte un corset depuis quinze jours.
'She has been wearing a brace for two weeks.' Catherine notes Noemie's neck brace. Notice how 'wears' leads directly into the noun meaning 'brace'.
Oui, elle doit bien se reposer.
'Yes, she needs to rest properly.' Mathias agrees on the necessity of recovery. The short 'self' word sits right in front of the verb for 'must', turning the action back onto the subject.
Je la trouve vraiment très rayonnante.
'I find her truly very radiant.' Catherine compliments Noemie's healthy appearance. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'find'.
C'est gentil d'être passée à l'agence.
'It is kind of you to stop by the agency.' Mathias acknowledges her visit politely. The verb meaning 'have' pairs naturally with the noun for 'agency' in everyday conversation.
Je l'ai invitée à dîner ce soir.
'I invited her to dinner tonight.' Catherine announces the dinner invitation. The verb meaning 'have' pairs naturally with the noun for 'evening' in everyday conversation.
Tu l'as invitée chez nous?
'You invited her to our place?' Mathias reacts with nervous surprise. Mathias uses the casual singular 'you' with 'have', showing close familiarity.
Oui, avec quelques amis très sympathiques.
'Yes, with a few very nice friends.' Catherine describes the guest list. The key noun here means 'friends', anchored by its matching French article.
Mon kiné Alexandre sera là aussi.
'My physiotherapist Alexandre will be there too.' Catherine mentions her physical therapist. The verb meaning 'will be' pairs naturally with the noun for 'physiotherapist' in everyday conversation.
Tu penses que c'est une bonne idée?
'Do you think that is a good idea?' Mathias questions the matchmaking scheme. Notice how 'think' leads directly into the noun meaning 'idea'.
Il est charmant et extrêmement doué.
'He is charming and extremely talented.' Catherine praises Alexandre's qualities. The descriptive adjective for 'charming' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Il va beaucoup l'aider pour sa rééducation.

'He will help her a lot with her rehabilitation.' Catherine justifies the match with therapeutic benefits. The verb meaning 'goes' pairs naturally with the noun for 'rehabilitation' in everyday conversation.
D'accord, nous verrons bien ce soir.

'Okay, we shall see tonight.' Mathias concedes with quiet hesitation. The verb meaning 'will see' pairs naturally with the noun for 'evening' in everyday conversation. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.
